{{short description|On convergent subsequences of regulated functions}}
In [[mathematics]], the '''Fraňková&ndash;Helly selection theorem''' is a generalisation of [[Helly's selection theorem]] for functions of [[bounded variation]] to the case of [[regulated function]]s. It was proved in 1991 by the [[Czech Republic|Czech]] [[mathematician]] [[Dana Fraňková]].

==Background==

Let ''X'' be a [[separable space|separable]] [[Hilbert space]], and let BV([0, ''T'']; ''X'') denote the [[normed vector space]] of all functions ''f'' : [0, ''T''] &rarr; ''X'' with finite total variation over the [[interval (mathematics)|interval]] [0, ''T''], equipped with the total variation norm. It is well known that BV([0, ''T'']; ''X'') satisfies the [[compact space|compactness theorem]] known as '''Helly's selection theorem''': given any sequence of functions (''f''<sub>''n''</sub>)<sub>''n''&isin;'''N'''</sub> in BV([0, ''T'']; ''X'') that is uniformly bounded in the total variation norm, there exists a subsequence

:<math>\left( f_{n(k)} \right) \subseteq (f_{n}) \subset \mathrm{BV}([0, T]; X)</math>

and a limit function ''f'' &isin; BV([0, ''T'']; ''X'') such that ''f''<sub>''n''(''k'')</sub>(''t'') [[Weak convergence (Hilbert space)|converges weakly]] in ''X'' to ''f''(''t'') for every ''t'' &isin; [0, ''T'']. That is, for every [[continuous linear functional]] ''&lambda;'' &isin; ''X''*,

:<math>\lambda \left( f_{n(k)}(t) \right) \to \lambda(f(t)) \mbox{ in } X \mbox{ as } k \to \infty.</math>

Consider now the [[Banach space]] Reg([0, ''T'']; ''X'') of all regulated functions ''f'' : [0, ''T''] &rarr; ''X'', equipped with the [[supremum norm]]. Helly's theorem does not hold for the space Reg([0, ''T'']; ''X''): a [[counterexample]] is given by the sequence

:<math>f_{n} (t) = \sin (n t).</math>

One may ask, however, if a weaker selection theorem is true, and the '''Fraňková&ndash;Helly selection theorem''' is such a result.

==Statement of the Fraňková&ndash;Helly selection theorem==

As before, let ''X'' be a separable Hilbert space and let Reg([0, ''T'']; ''X'') denote the space of regulated functions ''f'' : [0, ''T''] &rarr; ''X'', equipped with the supremum norm. Let (''f''<sub>''n''</sub>)<sub>''n''&isin;'''N'''</sub> be a sequence in Reg([0, ''T'']; ''X'') satisfying the following condition: for every ''ε'' &gt; 0, there exists some ''L''<sub>ε</sub> &gt; 0 so that each ''f''<sub>''n''</sub> may be approximated by a ''u''<sub>''n''</sub> &isin; BV([0, ''T'']; ''X'') satisfying

:<math>\| f_{n} - u_{n} \|_{\infty} < \varepsilon</math>

and

:<math>| u_{n}(0) | + \mathrm{Var}(u_{n}) \leq L_{\varepsilon},</math>

where |-| denotes the [[norm (mathematics)|norm]] in ''X'' and Var(''u'') denotes the variation of ''u'', which is defined to be the [[supremum]]

:<math>\sup_{\Pi} \sum_{j=1}^{m} | u(t_{j}) - u(t_{j-1}) |</math>

over all [[partition of an interval|partitions]]

:<math>\Pi = \{ 0 = t_{0} < t_{1} < \dots < t_{m} = T , m \in \mathbf{N} \}</math>

of [0, ''T'']. Then there exists a subsequence

:<math>\left( f_{n(k)} \right) \subseteq (f_{n}) \subset \mathrm{Reg}([0, T]; X)</math>

and a limit function ''f'' &isin; Reg([0, ''T'']; ''X'') such that ''f''<sub>''n''(''k'')</sub>(''t'') converges weakly in ''X'' to ''f''(''t'') for every ''t'' &isin; [0, ''T'']. That is, for every continuous linear functional ''&lambda;'' &isin; ''X''*,

:<math>\lambda \left( f_{n(k)}(t) \right) \to \lambda(f(t)) \mbox{ in } \mathbb{R} \mbox{ as } k \to \infty.</math>
